lines.text: So, now that the company's reconsidering remote work, where do you stand on it?
Honestly, I'm a bit torn. On the one hand, not commuting has given me back nearly two hours a day.
That's hardly trivial. But I'd argue we've lost something in terms of team cohesion.
I take your point. Spontaneous conversations by the coffee machine are surprisingly hard to replicate online.
Exactly. And for new hires it's even tougher — they're expected to pick things up without anyone to shadow.
Admittedly, that's a fair criticism. Having said that, I'm not convinced forcing everyone back five days a week is the answer.
No, that would probably backfire. People have got used to the flexibility.
What I'd propose is a hybrid model — say, two anchor days when the whole team is in.
That sounds reasonable, provided the days are coordinated. Otherwise you end up in the office on Zoom calls all day.
Ha, yes — the worst of both worlds. It'd need some discipline from managers.
Well, if you put it together as a proposal, I'd be happy to back it.
Great. I'll draft something and send it round by Friday.
